report.source_text: OCT imaging (Fig. 3, 4) showed a closed macular defect and residual postoperative tissue reorganization. The best-corrected visual acuity improved to 0.3 three months postoperatively.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 6-year-old patient presented with sudden vision loss (BCVA 0.02) in the right eye following blunt ocular trauma, accompanied by anterior segment disruption (hyphema, corneal edema, post-traumatic uveitis, diminished red reflex). On admission, indirect fundoscopy and OCT confirmed a full-thickness macular rupture (E001). The patient was observed conservatively for three months, during which BCVA remained unchanged at 0.02 and OCT demonstrated a stable macular defect (E002). At three months post-injury, the patient underwent pars plana vitrectomy with internal limiting membrane peeling using the inverted flap technique and 20% SF6 gas tamponade (E003). Three months postoperatively, OCT showed anatomical closure of the macular defect with residual postoperative tissue reorganization, and BCVA improved to 0.3 (E004).
